title: Procedure for the Development of Multi-depth Circular Cross-sectional Endothelialized Microchannels-on-a-chip
protocol: Transfer reflow photoresist from refrigerator to cleanroom 24 hours before use.
Allow reflow photoresist to warm to room temperature.
Clean silicon wafer thoroughly.
Bake silicon wafer at 150 °C for one hour to dehydrate and improve adhesion of photoresist.
Spin-coat first layer of photoresist using specified recipe.
Bake wafer on hotplate at 110 °C for 90 seconds (soft bake).
Spin-coat second layer of photoresist using the same recipe as first layer.
Bake wafer again on hotplate at 110 °C for 90 seconds (soft bake).
Expose photoresist to UV light with an exposure dose of 14,500 mJ/cm² through a film mask.
Dilute the developer with deionized (DI) water at a ratio of 1:2 (v/v).
Rinse the wafer repeatedly in the diluted developer solution until the pattern is fully developed.
Wash the wafer with DI water.
Dry the wafer using nitrogen gas.
Place the wafer on a hotplate at a temperature of 120 °C for 4 min, covering it with a glass Petri dish to prevent solvent evaporation.
Remove the wafer from the hotplate and allow it to cool to room temperature.
Prepare polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) solution at a weight ratio of 10:1 (base:curing agent).
Mix the PDMS thoroughly using a planetary centrifugal mixer.
Cast the PDMS solution onto the reflowed photoresist master mold.
Place the casted PDMS in a desiccator for 15 min to degas.
Use nitrogen gas to remove any remaining bubbles if necessary.
Bake the PDMS in an oven at a temperature of 60 °C for 3 hr to allow it to cure.
Remove the cured PDMS layer from the master mold.
Create inlet/outlet holes by punching holes in the channel network using a sharpened puncher.
Clean the surface of the PDMS using nitrogen gas.
Treat two PDMS layers with oxygen plasma for 30 sec inside a plasma cleaner at an operating pressure of 4.5 x 10^-2 Torr and an oxygen flow rate of 3.5 ft^3/min.
Align the surfaces of the PDMS manually under an optical microscope.
Use a drop of water if necessary to better control the alignment.
Bake the device in an oven at 60 °C for 30 min to achieve permanent bonding.
Culture HUVECs with culture medium supplemented with L-glutamine and 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Harvest confluent HUVECs by rinsing cells with HEPES buffered saline solution (HEPES-BSS).
Treat the harvested cells with trypsin/EDTA and incubate for 2-6 min at 37 °C.
Neutralize trypsin/EDTA treatment with trypsin neutralizing solution.
Centrifuge the cells and suspend them in culture medium containing 8% dextran.
Treat the device with oxygen plasma for 5 min at an operating pressure of 4.5 x 10^-2 Torr and an oxygen flow rate of 3.5 ft^3/min.
Load the device with DI water and treat it with UV light for 8 hr in a laminar biosafety hood for sterilization.
Wash the device with 1x phosphate buffered saline (1x PBS) one day before cell seeding.
Coat the device with fibronectin at a concentration of 100 μg/ml, diluted with 1x PBS.
Incubate the coated device in the refrigerator at 4 °C overnight.
Wash the device with 1x PBS after fibronectin coating is complete.
Load the device with culture medium and incubate it at 37 °C for 15 min.
Load the HUVEC cells in 8% dextran culture medium with a cell concentration of 3-4 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Place a 20 μl droplet of cells at one inlet of the device and tilt it to introduce the cells into the microfluidic channel.
Rotate the device every 15 min to create a more uniform distribution of cells.
Set up perfusion using a remote controlled syringe pump system with a steady flow of 10 μl/hr after static culture for 5-6 hr.
Wash the device with 1x PBS when HUVECs reach confluence inside the device.
Load the device with red dye diluted with diluent (4 μl-1 ml).
Incubate the device in the dark for 5 min at room temperature.
Thoroughly wash the device with culture medium to stop the staining.
Load the device with blue dye diluted with 1x PBS (2 droplets per ml).
Incubate in the dark for 5 min at room temperature.
Thoroughly wash the device with 1x PBS.
Examine the cell staining under an inverted optical microscope.
Load the microchannels with fixing medium (3.5% paraformaldehyde diluted with 1x PBS).
Submerge the device in fixing medium and cover it completely with aluminum foil.
Store the fixed device in the refrigerator at a temperature of 4 °C to prevent drying out and photobleaching.
Prepare the fixed device for confocal imaging using a laser scanning confocal microscope.
